title: Safe mode and trust in extensions
goal: Explain safe-mode and extension-admission boundaries without running unknown code on the host.
prerequisites: onec.p9; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Each has a context and protection boundary.
Actual input/output and exact own source identified; unperformed stages marked NOT RUN.
Accepted original preserved; rejection and its limits explained.
sections: Rights constrain user operations, safe mode specific code capabilities, server profiles additional server resources, andVMsan environment boundary. They are not interchangeable. A directive or checkbox does not prove host-file protection against arbitrary configuration modules. Define threat and supported context first.

Separate application roles, platform safe mode and OS isolation. Each controls a different boundary; none alone proves an arbitrary file safe. The beginner route remains ordinary installed official training 1C.

Execute/Evalon user input turns data into a program. Prefer a constrained operation language with explicit validation. Where dynamic execution is required under an official contract, safe mode also needs callable-function restrictions. Do not proposeevalas a universal adapter forStudio code inside a trusted configuration.

Review own extension/processor source and dependencies for dynamic execution, file/network effects, privilege, external components and metadata changes. A keyword alone is not proof of a vulnerability; document required effects and justified admission/refusal.

Bind an original teaching extension to a base configuration, version and hash. Check borrowed objects, changed methods and preservation after disabling. Compatibility with one version does not cover all upgrades. Exclude proprietary solutions and never execute unknown files merely to obtain PASS.

Use no malicious sample. A fictional card with unknown origin, arbitrary host/privilege requirements and no source must yield NOT RUN. Pure own calculations use minimal inputs and validated ranges rather than global privilege.

Use synthetic canaries and a disposable permitted environment without real secrets. Test prohibited files, network, process creation and output limits under the chosen model. Untested boundaries remainPLANNED/NOTRUN. Source hashes prove unchanged bytes, not a complete threat model or protected learner grading.

Actual safe-mode testing needs the exact version, licensed environment, reviewed own code and a specified allowed operation/rejection. Until run it remains PLANNED. Remove untested protection promises from instructions and acceptance records.
